Samira —

Thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front, followed by attachments/links and a technical appendix that Karthik will add to:

1) BYOK import transit encryption: we use RSA-OAEP (SHA-256) for wrapping customer key material. For symmetric keys we recommend AES-256 wrapping; for asymmetric imports the envelope uses RSA-OAEP with 4096-bit keys by default for strong import use cases. You can find the sample import commands in the attached byok-import-sample-commands.txt.

2) HSM attestation & key ceremony: Redwood runs customer keys on FIPS 140-2/3 validated modules (varies by deployment — we include vendor and model in the attestation PDF). We provide signed HSM attestation packages which include: module certs, HSM firmware hashes, and a redacted key ceremony log showing participating operators and timestamps. See redwood_hsm_attestation_2026-09-01.pdf attached.

3) TLS profiles: client-facing APIs require TLS1.3. We accept TLS1.2 for legacy mutual-TLS (mTLS) endpoints in dedicated/private deployments, but mandate AEAD ciphers with PFS. Minimum accepted suites: TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256, TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384, and CHACHA20_POLY1305 for TLS1.3; for TLS1.2: TLS_ECDHE_RSA_WITH_AES_128_GCM_SHA256 and TLS_ECDHE_RSA_WITH_AES_256_GCM_SHA384. We reject CBC-mode ciphers and anonymous DH.

Attachments: redwood_hsm_attestation_2026-09-01.pdf (attestation bundle), byok-import-sample-commands.txt, rotation-playbook-2026.pdf, key-lineage-sample.csv.

Karthik will follow up with more specifics about key lineage hashes and KMIP compatibility. If Helios wants a short walk-through call to review the attestation package, we can set one up tomorrow morning.

Samira — adding a few technical details to the summary Grace sent so it maps to Helios security checklist items: 

- BYOK import flow: we support both online import (customer generates key locally, we provide a one-time import token; client-side wraps the key with RSA-OAEP/SHA-256) and offline import (customer uploads wrapped envelope via a secure portal). The wrapped envelope includes a header with a key_id and a SHA-256 hash of the raw key material — we store the hash to provide lineage proof without storing raw key bytes.

- Key material provenance / chain-of-custody: our platform computes and records a deterministic provenance record for every imported key: {import_timestamp, importer_identity, wrapping_algorithm, envelope_hash}. For evidence we can provide a CSV extract (key-lineage-sample.csv) with redacted key identifiers and signature timestamps. Every provenance record is signed by Redwood's key-management service using an internal signing key so you can verify integrity.

- HSM integration: we operate multiple HSM backends depending on deployment: (1) cloud-vendor HSMs (HSM modules in public clouds with vendor attestations), (2) Redwood-managed FIPS HSM clusters for Dedicated customers, (3) customer-provided HSMs in Private deployments. Attestations include vendor/model, serial ranges, FIPS validation, and an HSM-generated quote where available. We do not export raw key material from an HSM unless explicitly requested under an agreed key-escrow process.

- KMIP & APIs: Key management operations are available via KMIP v2.0 for dedicated/private deployments and via a REST import/export API for hosted flows. Access controls support RBAC with separation of duties — key export/export operations require multiple role approvals and are logged.

- Rotation policy: default service-key rotation is automated at 90 days; recommended customer-managed key rotation (BYOK) is 365 days, but we can configure to meet Helios policy (30/90/365). Rotation events are recorded in the provenance log and linked to the key-id.

- TLS internals: Service-to-service uses mTLS with mutual authentication, TLS1.3 preferred. We also support TLS delegation to a load balancer that terminates TLS with HSTS and OCSP stapling enabled. Cipher suites and TLS versions are configurable per deployment; we can lock endpoints to Helios-mandated suites.

If you need, we can provide a signed digest of the HSM attestation bundle (SHA-256) and a redacted key ceremony timeline. I have attached a sample digest and the rotation playbook.

-Karthik
